items.text: Incorporated all 3 resolved decisions from round 2 into conclusion.md: (1) synchronous-with-timeout endpoint behavior — POST blocks and returns inline for typical commits, falls back to scan-run ID polling at 10s; (2) AES-256-GCM application-level encryption for watchlist values with server key from environment variable; (3) tiered PII severity classification — SSN/CC=critical, email/phone=high, IP/path=medium, custom watchlist=high.

Updated conclusion summary to reflect all 6 resolved design decisions across rounds 1 and 2. Added findings 9 (sync-with-timeout behavior), 10 (tiered severity), and expanded finding 8 (encryption details). Updated finding 11 schema to note AES-256-GCM for watchlist. Actions section now carries forward all 6 decisions with round/option references.

Remaining gaps not addressable through workshop: (1) performance benchmarking of pattern matching on large file lists — requires implementation and profiling; (2) false-positive rates for generic PII regex — requires testing against real codebases; (3) encryption key rotation/backup procedures — deferred to implementation; (4) RBAC for watchlist management — no auth system exists yet in secrets-manager. These are implementation-time concerns, not design blockers.

Readiness assessment: problem_clarity=3 (fully understood — research question answered with 11 detailed findings), scope_defined=3 (acceptance_allow set, API contracts defined, DB schema specified, all design decisions resolved), approach_solid=3 (concrete strategy with 6 resolved decisions covering endpoint behavior, storage, encryption, severity, and allowlist granularity), testable=2 (test cases identifiable from API contracts and schema but no formal test plan written — deferred to execute item), risk_awareness=2 (key risks noted in limitations but no formal mitigation matrix — performance and false-positive risks require implementation to resolve).
